evidence.quote: We propose a $40 million class fund, distributed automatically to the identified members, plus $7 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval.
We propose a $28 million class fund plus up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses.
We are open to discussing the allocation within Brightline’s $40 million all-in limit.
The fee is subject to court scrutiny and should not be increased at the class’s expense.

summary: Plaintiff first raised fees in its opening public proposal, before class relief was settled. Fees and class relief were negotiated together, and the transcript contains explicit linkage through an all-in cap/allocation discussion and counsel’s statement that fees should not be increased at the class’s expense. There is no clear evidence that plaintiff prioritized firm fees over the class, that defense exploited fee interests, or that the court declaration was misleading.
